# 2026-09-03 — Session 18 — LEG-041 `branch_id` correction: autogenerated slot identity

## Scope

Correct a design/spec/code drift in the parallel fan-in slot identity. The
maintainer ruled (journal 2026-09-01, session 15u) that `branch_id` is an
**autogenerated** slot identity: present from the flow start, **constant along a
branch's sequence**, and **distinct per branch at the same level of the same
task** — so two branches that are the very same class/sequence still occupy two
distinct join slots of that one task. It is generated only by the submit/flow
starter and by the parallel. The session-17 implementation (and the specs/design
that mirrored it) instead set `branch_id` to the **branch class name**, which
causes two same-class branches of one task to collide on the same join slot.
This session realigns docs, design files, code and tests to the ruling.

## Work done (per concern)

Note: per the maintainer's direction, this correction was made **docs/design
files first, then code** — the reverse of implementation.

- **`docs/CONTRACTS/LEG-041-parallel-agent.md`** — rewrote the fan-in identity
  block: `branch_id` is now described as **autogenerated by the parallel at
  fan-out**, preserved unchanged through the branch's whole execution, constant
  along the branch's sequence, and distinct per branch at the same level of the
  same task. Stated that two branches that are the same class/sequence still
  occupy two distinct join slots of one task; generated only by submit and
  parallel. Removed the "branch class name" formulation and the false
  "each branch is one child task" claim.
- **`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §3** — field list entry for `branch_id` updated to
  the autogenerated/constant-per-branch/distinct-per-branch semantics; the
  Parallel (branching) bullet now assigns an autogenerated `branch_id`
  (distinct per branch at this level) instead of `= the branch class name`.
- **`docs/AGENT_LIFECYCLE.md` §4.11** — settled-token table `branch_id` row and
  the Parallel (branching) bullet updated to the autogenerated semantics
  (distinct per branch, constant along the branch's sequence, preserved).
- **`docs/CONTRACTS/LEG-042-fanin-gathering-queue.md`** — removed the invented
  "canonical hole resolution / departure gate / gate follow-on" model and the
  **delegation to LEG-052** (`[per LEG-052]` acceptance criterion + the
  agent-name regression tests), per the maintainer's standing rule to eliminate
  out-of-design content and delegations. The spec now states the actual design:
  slot-stable join per (parallel, task, branch slot) keyed on the constant
  `task_id` with slot identity from the autogenerated `branch_id`; exactly-once
  join; visible failure for a missing/bugged branch; advance-then-delete
  ordering.
- **`src/legio/flow/messages.py`** — module docstring for the `branch_id` token
  field reworded to the autogenerated/constant/distinct semantics.
- **`src/legio/agents/parallel_agent.py`** — `_fan_out` now mints an
  autogenerated per-branch slot id (`<task_id>:<agent_id>:<index>`) and keys the
  join slots dict on it (no longer on the branch class name); `_fan_in`
  resolves the slot directly by the result's `branch_id` (dropped the
  `level_route[0]` fallback); module + `_fan_in` docstrings updated. The
  preservation through advance / sequence re-seed / parallel resume is
  unchanged (that was correct — `branch_id` is constant along a branch).
- **`tests/test_leg041_parallel_agent.py`** — updated to the autogenerated slot
  identity: children are read back after fan-out to obtain their `branch_id`
  and return it on their results; added
  `test_parallel_two_same_class_branches_get_distinct_branch_ids` — two branches
  of the very same class in one task get distinct `branch_id`s (the case the
  class-name implementation broke).

## Logging added

No new runtime events: the parallel still emits `parallel fan-out` /
`parallel partial` / `parallel joined`; the fan-out INFO line now also logs the
per-branch `branch` slot id (observability of the slot identity, rule 11). No
lifecycle point was added or removed.

## Tests run

- `uv run python -m pytest tests/test_leg041_parallel_agent.py -q` → **7 passed**
  (includes the new same-class-branch distinctness test).
- `uv run python -m pytest -q` → **129 passed** (was 128).
- `uv run ruff check src tests` → **All checks passed**.
- `uv run pyright` → **0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 informations**.

## Decisions taken

- `branch_id` is the **autogenerated parallel branch slot identity**: minted by
  the parallel at fan-out (and by the submit for a branch-starting flow), valid
  only to distinguish the slots of one constant `task_id`. It is **not** the
  branch class name; two same-class branches of one task are two distinct slots.
- `branch_id` is preserved unchanged through a branch's advance / sequence
  re-seed / parallel resume (constant along the branch's sequence).
- No fallback to `level_route[0]` in the fan-in — slot is named exclusively by
  the preserved `branch_id`.
- LEG-042 no longer delegates to LEG-052 nor describes a non-existent
  hole/departure-gate model; it specifies the actual slot-stable, exactly-once
  join and visible-failure behavior.

## Known issues / open points

- The same-class distinctness is now covered by contract test; the LEG-052
  (R-5) issue remains separately scoped (path-based fan-in identity) and is not
  touched here.
- Journals 2026-09-02 (sessions 17/17b) record the previous class-name
  implementation; those historical entries are not edited.

## Next steps

- Commit this correction (journal within the turn, rule 3; the work tree with
  it as it is now final/stable).
- Await maintainer review of the realigned `branch_id` semantics before further
  R-4 work (LEG-043 composite examples).

# 2026-09-03 — Session 19 — LEG-043 composite examples (sequence + parallel root) green end-to-end

## Scope

Finish LEG-043: two in-repo, domain-free composite examples proven green
end-to-end over the REST mini-manager (LEG-025/LEG-027), exercising the R-4
engine on real beaver through the decoupled polling model.

The maintainer confirmed during the turn: *a parallel can be a starting agent;
every agent can be a starting agent*. This anchors the parallel-root delivery
path: submit is a dumb delivery point that hands the task to the starting
agent's own class queue; the ParallelAgent concretizes the fan-out itself. It
also corrected an implementation misstep: I had improvised against the pinned
LEG-010 test instead of anchoring to the design — fixed by realigning the test
to the design rather than the reverse.

## Work done

- **`src/legio/patterns/sequences.py`**: `starting_route` now returns `(spec.name,)`
  for a parallel root (it is a starting agent) instead of raising
  `UnrecoverableError`; docstring updated (atomic → own class, parallel root →
  own class, `main` sequence still flattened, nested composite inside a
  sequence still raises).
- **`tests/test_leg010_patterns_schema.py`**: obsolete
  `test_starting_route_rejects_parallel` realigned to
  `test_starting_route_starts_parallel_root_on_its_own_class`, asserting
  `starting_route(distribute_summary) == ("distribute_summary",)`.
- **`tests/test_leg043_examples_composites.py`** (NEW): two contract tests —
  - `test_extract_and_summarize_sequence_over_rest`: a **sequence** root
    (linguistic `extract` → tool `assess`) driven via `POST /submit` +
    `GET /status`; the linguistic uses lingo with a compiled `ExtractOutput`
    pydantic model, the tool consumes `{extract.title}`/`{extract.summary}`.
  - `test_distribute_summary_parallel_root_over_rest`: a **parallel** root over
    REST; submit delivers to the parallel's own class, `ParallelAgent.run()`
    fans out to `summ`/`cata` linguistic branches, branches run to a standstill,
    parallel builds its payload on all-complete. Asserts `output.summ`/`output.cata`.

## Logging added

- No new modules/events beyond what already shipped. The examples rely on the
  existing per-agent INFO logs (tool declare, manager create/close, agent
  poll/route) verified via `caplog` in both tests. No rettooling needed.

## Tests run

- `uv run python -m pytest -q` → **131 passed**.
- `uv run ruff check src tests` → all checks passed.
- `uv run pyright` → **0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 informations**.
- Validation cases (the two LEG-043 examples over REST) → **both green**.

## Decisions taken

- A parallel root is a valid starting agent: `starting_route` yields its own
  class name; the ParallelAgent resolves the fan-out. This is the decoupled
  (rule 1) path — the submit never reads the parallel's structure.
- LEG-010's pin that parallel raises in `starting_route` was obsolete (R-3-era)

- Branch bindings in a parallel bind from the parallel's entry (`input_as`), so
  the distribute example uses linguistic branches (prompt vars from the branch's
  own `input_schema`), consistent with the existing LEG-010 `PARALLEL_YAML`.

  examples keep per-branch output keys distinct so the current build is correct.
- LEG-042 remains DRAFT awaiting approval.

## Next steps

# 2026-09-03 — Session 20 — payload is construction, not accumulation: re-keying between agents + flow contract (conceptual, docs-only)

## Scope

The maintainer corrected a deep conceptual drift in how the payload travels and
how the flow contract is defined. This turn is **docs-only** (no code): the
correct model was clarified through several correction rounds, and the flow
contract was finally defined. It ends mid-design so the machine could be shut
down; the next turn resumes from here.

## What the maintainer ruled (verbatim spirit, consolidated)

1. **input_as / output_as are properties of the agent** (declared in its spec,
   Schema 1, both mandatory). `output_as` is **internal to the agent** and never
   travels; `input_as` is the key under which the agent looks up its input.
2. **The payload does NOT accumulate.** It is a **construction** in a chain: each
   agent has an `input_as` (a subset of what the previous agent produced), builds
   its own output, and hands its output to the next. No "union", no accumulation.
   (My earlier "union"/"merge" and "keeps every earlier step's keys" ideas were
   wrong and were corrected.)
3. **Re-keying (cambio de clave) between agents.** Because each agent is defined
   independently, its `output_as` differs from the next agent's `input_as`. So
   whoever hands the task to the next agent re-keys the produced value under the
   next agent's `input_as`. `build_payload` builds the payload however the agent
   understands and delivers it under `output_as`; **the one who assembles the
   final schema queued for the next agent does the re-keying** (remapping).
4. **The route carries only `class` and `input_as`** per position (the
   information the re-keying needs); `output_as` is internal and does not travel.
   `level_route` becomes a tuple of `(class, input_as)`.
5. **The submit re-keys the client payload under the starting agent's `input_as`.**
6. **The flow contract (defined this turn):** the flow's input is the `input_as`
   of the **starting agent** (first agent of level 1); the flow's output is the
   `output_as` of the **last agent of the main (level-1) sequence**. Every
   intermediate `output_as` is only an internal bridge to the next agent, not
   part of the client's request nor of the final result.
7. **Process for the changes:** the maintainer asked to go **step by step** — do
   one plan step, describe it, wait for authorization — and to **rewrite** the
   documentation to the correct model (not leave confusing change-notes), docs
   before code (AGENTS.md rule 12).

## Work done

- **Docs only.** Rewrote `docs/AGENT_LIFECYCLE.md` §12.1 ("The message payload
  is the state") to the construction model:
  - each agent declares `input_as`/`output_as` as its own aliases;
  - the payload does not accumulate — it is rebuilt (re-keyed) at every hop;
  - the route (`level_route`) carries `(class, input_as)` per position; the
    `output_as` is internal and never travels;
  - the submit re-keys the client payload under the starting agent's `input_as`;
  - the **flow contract** anchored to level-1 ends: input = starting agent's
    `input_as`, output = last agent of level 1's `output_as`.
- No code touched yet. This is the first (documentation) plan step.

## Logging added

- None (docs only).

## Tests run

- Not run this turn (no code change). The suite was green at the last code
  commit (`109a152`, 131 passed, ruff clean, pyright 0 errors).

## Decisions taken

- The full payload-construction model above (points 1-6). This must be carried
  forward into the remaining plan steps (docs + code).

## Known issues / open points — RESUME HERE

- The following plan steps remain, to be done **one at a time with maintainer
  authorization** (docs first, then code):
  1. ✅ (this turn) AGENT_LIFECYCLE §12.1 rewritten; flow contract defined.
  2. Rewrite AGENT_LIFECYCLE §12.4 fan-in parallel (builds payload; re-keying;
     still uses `output_as` namespacing per branch — review wording for
     "namespacing", which may itself be wrong terminology).
  3. Rewrite ARCHITECTURE references and the contracts LEG-040/041/042/043/032 to
     the construction+re-keying model (no union/accumulation).
  4. Code: `build_payload` — namespace mandatory; builds `{output_as: output}`
     (construction, not accumulation). `output` and `namespace` are NOT loose
     arguments-to-be-invented; `output_as` is a property of the agent.
  5. Code: extend `level_route` to `tuple[(class, input_as), ...]` in
     `messages.py`.
  6. Code: re-keying when enqueuing the next request (in `AgentBase._route_outcome`),
     using `level_route[next][1]` (`input_as` of the next); `output_as` internal.
  7. Code: submit re-keys client payload under the starting agent's `input_as`.
  8. Code: update `sequences.py`, `SequenceAgent`, `ParallelAgent`, and the
     `build_payload` callers (tool/linguistic/parallel) to the new model.
  9. Update all tests to the new route/re-keying; suite green.
  10. Journal + commit.
- Open design detail still to confirm when resumed: how exactly the final result
  payload is presented to the client (the last agent of level 1 produces under
  its `output_as`; the result queue receives it — confirm whether it stays under
  that `output_as` or is re-keyed once more for the response; the flow contract
  says the output is the last level-1 agent's `output_as`).

# 2026-09-03 — Session 21 — Structural redesign: only `composite` with `branches` (no sequence/parallel kinds); flow output = starting agent's output_as

## Scope

The maintainer directed a structural simplification of the agent model and
closed the flow-contract definition left open in Session 20. **Analysis only,
no implementation.** The machine was powered off mid-turn before (Session 20);
this session is the consolidated, carry-forward design state.

## What the maintainer ruled (consolidated)

1. **The flow output is the starting agent's own `output_as`**, not "the last
   agent of level 1". Rationale: an atomic is a single agent (no chaining); a
   composite ramifies and, on fan-in, **builds its own final output**. In every
   case the starting agent is the one that produces the flow's output.
2. **No `sequence` and no `parallel` as separate `kind`s — only `composite`.**
   A `composite` has `branches`:
   - `composite` with **1 branch** models what used to be `sequence` (linear).
   - `composite` with **N branches** (>1) models what used to be `parallel`.
   - **Each branch is a sequence of agents**, and each agent in that sequence may
     be atomic or composite (recursive → a real tree / DAG of arbitrary depth).
3. **The composite maps its branches exactly like the parallel did** — same
   mechanism, no special behavior for the 1-branch case. It ramifies to its
   branches, gathers the fan-in on its gathering queue, and **constructs its
   `output_as`** by mapping the branch results exactly as the parallel mapped
   them. One code path, one runner.
4. Re-keying (change of key) applies at every hop, identically: entering an agent
   (under its `input_as`), advancing within a branch's sequence, and when the
   composite gathers its branches to build its output.

## Analysis (this session)

- Unifying sequence+parallel into composite removes the `SequenceAgent` /
  `ParallelAgent` duality and the `sequence:`/`parallel:` schema fields, with a
  single composite runner (ramify → gather → build). "Sequence" and "parallel"
  become just the arity (1 vs N) of the composite.
- The earlier open question (sequence output == last agent's output, an
  invariant to control, vs the last agent depositing into a starting-agent queue)
  is **nullified by the unification**: the composite ALWAYS builds its own
  `output_as` after gathering, whether it has 1 or N branches. No exception, no
  special invariant.
- The flow contract is now clean and uniform: **input = starting agent's
  `input_as`; output = starting agent's `output_as`**, for atomic, composite
  (any arity), and recursive nesting.
- Current schema has `AgentKind.SEQUENCE` / `AgentKind.PARALLEL` and
  `sequence:`/`parallel:` fields (schema1.py) — these will be replaced by a
  single composite-with-branches model. The parallel fan-in code (gathering,
  branch slots, build) is the template for the unified composite.

## Work done

- None (analysis only). No code, no further doc edits this session beyond the
  Session 20 §12.1 rewrite already committed (`4ad3021`).

## Logging added

- None.

## Tests run

- None (analysis only). Suite green at last code commit `109a152`.

## Decisions taken

- The structural redesign above (only `composite` with `branches`; flow output =
  starting agent's `output_as`; composite maps branches exactly like the
  parallel). This supersedes the "(class, input_as) level_route" note as the
  surrounding model — the re-keying idea remains valid, now applied uniformly
  over a recursive composite tree.
- Draft pending questions to confirm before implementing (see next section).

## Known issues / open points — RESUME HERE

- **NOT IMPLEMENTED.** The following design questions remain open and must be
  confirmed with the maintainer before any code:
  1. Exact YAML shape of the new `composite`: how `branches` are declared and how
     each branch expresses its ordered sequence of agents (e.g. `branches:[{steps:[...]}]`
     vs a single `steps:` on the composite; and whether the composite keeps `sequence:`/`parallel:`
     or collapses to one `branches:` field).
  2. Whether `kind` remains for tools/linguistic (tool|linguistic) and the
     composite is expressed purely by `type: composite` + a `branches` interior
     (dropping `kind: sequence|parallel`).
  3. How the composite maps branch results into its `output_as` (per-branch
     `output_as` projection, by position, or a build function) — to be specified
     as "exactly like the parallel" but pinned down concretely.
  4. Re-keying at ramification: how the composite's `input_as` payload reaches
     each branch's first agent (re-keyed under that branch's first step's
     `input_as`?), and how an N-branch composite shares its input.
  5. Whether "sequence as one branch" keeps a gathering queue / builds its output,
     or gets the forward-only optimization (the maintainer said the composite
     maps exactly like the parallel, implying it DOES gather and build — confirm).
  6. Migration of existing specs/examples/tests (LEG-032/040/041/042/043) from
     `kind: sequence|parallel` to the unified composite model.
  7. Docs to rewrite: AGENT_LIFECYCLE §12.3/§12.4, contracts LEG-040/041/042/043/032,
     ARCHITECTURE — to the unified composite model (still ahead of any code,
     per AGENTS.md rule 12).

## Next steps

- Resume by confirming the open questions (1-7) with the maintainer, then do the
  DESIGN DOCUMENTS first (rewrite to the unified composite model), then the code
  (schema, composite runner, re-keying), one authorized step at a time, keeping
  the suite green.

# 2026-09-03 — Session 22 — Plan for the composite-unification design variation (registered)

## Scope

The maintainer directed a structural design variation (only `composite` with
`branches`; no `sequence`/`parallel` kinds) and, on review, stressed a
recurring process failure: **I implement without following the defined
specifications**, producing code that does not match what was requested. This
session registers the concrete plan for the variation and, per the process the
maintainer enforces, each phase is **discussed before it is executed** — docs
first (AGENTS.md rule 12), then code, one authorized step at a time.

## Preliminary finding (implementation drift to fix)

- `ParallelAgent._fan_out` (`src/legio/agents/parallel_agent.py:95-115`)
  deposits each branch as a **single class**: `level_route=(branch_class,)`.
  This contradicts the specification in `docs/AGENT_LIFECYCLE.md` §12.4
  ("it fans out giving each branch its `level_route`") and
  `docs/CONTRACTS/LEG-041-parallel-agent.md` ("a composite/multi-step branch
  whose returned `level_route` expands to its own internal steps ... its
  `level_route[0]` would be the branch's first step, not the branch slot"). A
  branch may be atomic (sequence of size 1), a sequence (multi-step), or another
  composite (recursive) — the code does not fan out each branch's own route.
  Fixing this is part of Fase 3 below.

## Plan (consolidated, per the maintainer's direction)

### Fase 0 — Anchor (AGENTS.md rules 10/12)
Re-read `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/AGENT_LIFECYCLE.md` §4.10/§11/§12, and
contracts LEG-040/041/042/043 so every plan step cites the specification it
satisfies. Never implement "whatever comes to mind" — implement what the docs
define.

### Fase 1 — Documentation (rewrite, do not annotate) — BEFORE code
1. AGENT_LIFECYCLE §4.10/§11 (Schema 1): `type: composite` with a `branches`
   field; drop `kind: sequence|parallel`; each branch is a sequence of agents
   (atomic or composite); an atomic agent is a sequence of size 1.
2. AGENT_LIFECYCLE §12.3/§12.4: the composite (1 or N branches) ramifies,
   depositing each branch's own expanded `level_route` (its internal steps) at
   `current_index=0`, `level+1`, `end_of_level_queue` = its gathering queue; it
   gathers and builds its `output_as`. A branch may be atomic / sequence /
   composite.
3. AGENT_LIFECYCLE §12.1: construction + re-keying (started in `4ad3021`) and
   the flow contract (input = starting agent's `input_as`; output = starting
   agent's `output_as`).
4. Contracts LEG-040/041/042/043/032 rewritten to the unified model.
5. ARCHITECTURE: Schema 1, composites, payload sections.

### Fase 2 — Specify the composite→output mapping (the critical gap)
Pin down how the composite builds its `output_as` from its branch results (each
branch produces under its `output_as`; the composite maps them — resolve
LEG-042 "namespacing" wording, which itself may be wrong terminology, and the
flat-union current behavior).

### Fase 3 — Code (after documentation is approved), one authorized step at a time
1. Schema 1 (`schema1.py`): `AgentKind` → `tool|linguistic|composite`;
   `branches` field; drop `sequence`/`parallel`.
2. Loader (`loader.py`): validate composites with `branches`; each branch is a
   sequence; build the DAG by levels/branches (not linear flat); carry
   re-keying info `(class, input_as)`.
3. Route builder / `starting_route`: build the starting route as a
   level/branch tree, not a flat flattening.
4. `CompositeAgent` (unifies SequenceAgent + ParallelAgent): ramify → gather →
   build; **fan-out deposits each branch's own `level_route`**, not
   `(branch_class,)`; supports atomic/sequence/composite branches;
   `branch_id` constant per slot; builds `output_as`.
5. `build_payload` (`payload.py`): `namespace` mandatory = agent's `output_as`;
   construction `{output_as: output}`; re-keying when enqueuing in
   `AgentBase._route_outcome`.
6. Route in `messages.py`: `level_route` = tuple of `(class, input_as)`.
7. Submit: re-key client payload under the starting agent's `input_as`.

# 2026-09-03 — Session 23 — Eliminate accumulation: construction + re-keying (code, per maintainer)

## Scope

The maintainer ordered (again, and this time executed): eliminate the
accumulation model and implement re-keying ("elimina lo de acumulación, porque
el rekeying hay que hacerlo"). Prior attempts (Session 19b) only renamed
docstrings and left the union semantic alive in `payload.py` and LEG-040 — a
verified process failure. This session implements the construction +
re-keying model from AGENT_LIFECYCLE §12.1 and Sessions 20/21 across source,
contracts and tests.

## What the maintainer ruled / objective

- The payload is **construction, not accumulation**: each agent reads under its
  `input_as`, builds its own output under its `output_as`, and the payload is
  re-keyed at every hop. `build_payload` produces exactly `{output_as: output}`.
- `level_route` becomes `(class, input_as)` per position.
- Submit re-keys the client payload under the starting agent's `input_as`.

## Work done (code)

- `src/legio/flow/payload.py`: `build_payload(output, *, output_as)` →
  `{output_as: output}`. Removed the incoming-payload union (`base.update`)
  and the optional namespace. Construction only, no accumulation.
- `src/legio/flow/messages.py`: `level_route` = `tuple[RouteStep, ...]` where
  `RouteStep = (class, input_as)`.
- `src/legio/agents/base.py`: added `output_as` to `AgentBase`; `_route_outcome`
  re-keys the produced value under the next step's `input_as` (`_rekey`);
  errors pass through untouched (never swallowed).
- `src/legio/agents/tool_agent.py` / `linguistic_agent.py`: take `input_as` +
  `output_as`; read input from `payload[self._input_as]`; build via
  `build_payload(output, output_as=self._output_as)`.
- `src/legio/agents/parallel_agent.py`: branches are `(class, input_as)`;
  fan-out re-keys the shared input under each branch's `input_as`; fan-in
  gathers branch results and constructs `{output_as: {...}}`.
- `src/legio/agents/sequence_agent.py`: `sequence_route` is
  `(class, input_as)`; re-keys to the first stage's `input_as`.
- `src/legio/manager/__init__.py` `submit`: re-keys the client payload under
  `route[0][1]` (the starting agent's `input_as`).
- `src/legio/patterns/sequences.py` `starting_route` and `src/legio/api.py`
  `_resolve_route`: return `(class, input_as)` routes.
- `docs/CONTRACTS/LEG-040-sequence-agent.md`: replaced the "keeps every earlier
  step's keys" accumulation paragraph with the construction + re-keying model.
- Updated 12 test files to the `(class, input_as)` route + construction/re-keyed
  payload semantics.

## Logging added

- No new logger calls were needed; existing key=value events remain. Routing
  change is internal to `_route_outcome`/`_rekey` (no new observable lifecycle
  point).

## Tests run

- `uv run python -m pytest tests/ -q` → **131 passed**.
- `uv run ruff check src tests` → all checks passed.
- `uv run pyright src tests` → 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 informations.

## Decisions taken

- Construction + re-keying is now implemented on the current
  (sequence/parallel) structure, per §12.1. The flow output is the level-1
  closer's `output_as` (Session 20 wording in §12.1), which matches the current
  non-unified architecture; the Session 21 "starting agent's output_as"
  correction belongs to the still-pending unified `composite` redesign and is
  NOT claimed as done here.

## Known issues / open points

- The unified composite-with-branches redesign (Session 21 open questions 1-7,
  Session 22 Fase 3 step 1-4) is still NOT implemented. This session only
  eliminated accumulation + re-keying on the current sequence/parallel model.

# 2026-09-03 — Session 24 — Fase 1 sub-step 1 (discussion) + sub-step 2 (Schema 1 rewritten)

## Scope

Advance LEG-044's Fase 1 (documentation, before code). Sub-step 1: settle the
full Schema 1 vocabulary with the maintainer. Sub-step 2: rewrite
AGENT_LIFECYCLE §4.10/§4.11 (Schema 1) and the LEG-044 plan note to the unified
`composite`-with-`branches` model.

## Vocabulary settled with the maintainer (Session 23-24 discussion)

- `name` is **mandatory** in every agent (toplevel and inline are not used;
  there are no inline definitions at all).
- `type: atomic | composite` is the root discriminator; `kind:` is only the
  interior of an atomic — `tool | linguistic`. A composite is `type: composite`
  + `branches`, and carries no `kind`.
- **No inline definitions, no nested `branches`.** Every agent is defined once
  as a `pattern`; a step is exactly `{pattern: <name>, input_as: <alias>}` and
  references a defined pattern. Inner ramification is expressed by a step whose
  `pattern` is itself a `type: composite` (reuse by reference, recursive).
- The step's `input_as` is **validated to equal** the referenced pattern's
  declared `input_as` (no free aliases).
- **No `output_as` on a step** — it is always the referenced agent's own
  (internal, never travels); hence the re-keying handoff.
- `parameters` dotted paths are **mandatorily explicit** as `{input_as}.{key}`
  — the agent's own declared `input_as` + a key of its `input_schema`; no
  implicit resolution against the input content. Maintainer: "en arg es
  mandatory poner input_as.key, quiero esa verbosidad." (Correction to my
  earlier wrong assumption that resolution was implicit.)
- Every agent (atomic and composite) declares the full entry + output triples
  (`input_as`/`input_type`/`input_schema` and `output_as`/`output_type`/
  `output_schema`).

## Work done (docs only — Fase 1, no code yet)

- `docs/AGENT_LIFECYCLE.md`:

    only `tool|linguistic`; `branches` list-of-steps; `parameters` explicit

    nested branches; rejection rules updated.

    `sequence`/`parallel` kinds, added `branches`, `name` mandatory, explicit
    `{input_as}.{key}`.
  - §4.10.2, §4.10.3 (terse call vocabulary → explicit `{input_as}.{key}`),
    §4.10.4 (Composites bullet), §4.10.5 (reuse/re-keying), §4.10.6 (composite
    output, no nested branches / composite-in-branch), §4.10.8 (static checks):

  - Kind binding map (`{"linguistic","tool"}` + `type: composite`).

# 2026-09-03 — Session 25 — Apply the bare-step-name correction across the schema docs

## Scope

The maintainer flagged two Schema-1 fragmentations: (1) I presented Schema 2's
`branch_id` (essential for fan-in) only late and piecemeal — corrected to show
the full Schema 2 vocabulary up front; (2) the key correction: **a step in a
composite's `branches` is a BARE pattern name — it carries no `input_as`/
`output_as`**. The `(class, input_as)` pair that a route needs is **not declared
in the agent definition**; the loader resolves it when it builds the DAG of each
level/branch (Schema 2). This session applies that correction across every
schema/token/architecture document.

## Vocabulary (final, after this session)

- Schema 1: a composite is `type: composite` + `branches`; each branch is an
  ordered list of **bare pattern names**; no inline, no nested `branches`;
  inner ramification = a step whose name references a `type: composite`. The
  `(class, input_as)` route pair is resolved by the loader (Schema 2), never
  declared in the agent. `parameters` dotted paths are explicit
  `{input_as}.{key}`.
- Schema 2: `level_route` = tuple of `(class, input_as)`; `branch_id` = a
  composite's branch slot, autogenerated at fan-out, constant along the branch,
  carried on the message; fan-in accounts one result per `branch_id`.

# 2026-09-03 — Session 25c — branch_id is autogenerated and never empty (Schema 2)

## Maintainer rulings folded in

1. **`branch_id` never empty**: every message of the flow carries one. At flow
   birth the **submit assigns the root `branch_id`** to the starting agent's
   request; you are always in a branch (atomic or composite), from the start.
2. **`branch_id` is autogenerated** to avoid unexpected name collisions — a
   unique, random id with **no parent-derived naming** (my C3 simulation wrongly
   proposed hierarchical prefixes like `B1a`/`B1b`; rejected). Each composite
   autogenerates fresh, independent ids for its child branches, distinct from its
   own and from every other branch across all levels; the fan-in joins by that
   id.

## Work done (docs only)

- AGENT_LIFECYCLE §4.11 Schema 2: `branch_id` table cell rewritten (autogenerated
  unique id, submit assigns root at flow birth, every message carries one,
  never empty, constant along the branch, used as fan-in join slot); added a
  "Submit assigns the root branch_id" bullet; Composite (branching) bullet
  tightened to "fresh, unique autogenerated branch_id (no parent-derived
  naming)".
- AGENT_LIFECYCLE §12.4: fan-out `branch_id` -> "fresh autogenerated, unique
  (no parent-derived), distinct across all levels".
- LEG-011: submit-assigns-root bullet + Composite branching wording.
- ARCHITECTURE: §3 `branch_id` definition + "Who builds it" (root branch_id) +
  Composite branching wording.

# 2026-09-03 — Session 26 — corrected flow simulation (branch_id autogenerated + never empty)

## Objective

Validate that the mechanism behaves as designed and that no problem shows up,
now that `branch_id` semantics are fixed (autogenerated unique id, root assigned
by the submit at flow birth, every message carries one, fan-in joins by id).
Domain-free dummy agents only; no code change.

## Cases traced (stressed on purpose)

A. **Atomic root starting agent** — no fan-out, direct final under root id. Clean.
B. **Composite root with a single branch** — child id distinct from root id;
   fan-in 1/1; final under root id. Clean.
C. **Nested composite as a step of a branch** — inner autogenerates its own leaf
   ids (distinct from the parent branch id), inner joins its own ids, outer joins
   its own single child id; final under root id. Clean.

## Findings

- No collisions between autogenerated ids (across levels), no double-count, no
  hang; each fan-in counts exactly its own child branch ids and every branch
  closes exactly once.
- The output delivered to the final queue is always the starting agent's
  `output_as`, under the root `branch_id` the submit assigned. Confirms the
  design as intended.
- No problem found. This validates the fixed semantics (Session 25c) and the
  Session 21 flow contract (starting agent's input_as/output_as define the flow).

## Next

- Fase 2: specify the composite -> `output_as` mapping (the fan-in "builds" its
  output; exact mapping still open — not "flat-union").
- Choose the autogeneration source for `branch_id` (id generator).
- Docs for Schema 2 are now framework-consistent; §12 remains to be finalized
  with the Fase 2 mapping.
